Rashi on Ketubot 14b:12:2.hebrew: אם רוב העיר - כשרין להשיא בנותיהן ואלמנותיהן לכהונה, שאין רוב בני העיר מן הפוסלין אשה לכהונה בביאתן, אף זו תינשא לכהונה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:12:2.english: If the majority of the city - [are] fit to marry off their daughters and their widows to the priesthood, since the majority of the townspeople are not among those who disqualify a woman from the priesthood through their intercourse, this [girl] too may marry into the priesthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:13:1.english: That he stated in accordance with whose [opinion] - that he requires a majority of [people of] unflawed lineage.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:13:2.english: Even with a majority of unfit [men] he also deems [her] fit - For he holds [the principle]: "Establish the woman upon her presumptive status."

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:13:3.hebrew: אמר ליה הכי אמר כו' - לעולם כרבי יהושע, והכא משום דאיכא תרי רובי לכשרות אכשרה, וכדרב יהודה. ולקמן מפרש טעמא ואזיל, מאי שנא תרי רובי מחד רובא:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:13:3.english: He said to him: This is what [Rav Yehuda] said, etc. - Actually, [he holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, and here, because there are two majorities toward fitness, he declared her fit, and [this is] in accordance with Rav Yehuda. And later on, [the Gemara] proceeds to explain the reason: what is the difference between two majorities and one majority?

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:1:1.hebrew: שמעתי כו' - לקמיה פריך, היינו תנא קמא, דתנא קמא נמי הכי אמר, דמשום דאין בה אחד מכל אלו העידו עליה להכשיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:1:1.english: I heard, etc. - Later on, [the Gemara] asks: This is [the same as] the first Tanna, for the first Tanna also said this — that because it has none of all these [uncertainties], they testified concerning it to declare [it] fit.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:3:1.hebrew: מכירין ישראל ממזרין שביניהן - וספק ממזר יש לך להכשיר, דאי ממזר הוה, מידע הוו ידעי ביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:3:1.english: Jews recognize the mamzerim among them - And you should declare an uncertain mamzer fit, for if he were a mamzer, they would have known about him.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:3:2.hebrew: ואין מכירין חללין שביניהן - וספק חלל יש לך לפסול. ולקמיה פריך: הא אמרת רישא "איזוהי אלמנת עיסה? כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל" — אלמא ספק חלל כשר:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:3:2.english: And they do not identify the ḥalalin among them - and [therefore] you should disqualify an uncertain ḥalal. And later [the Gemara] asks: Did you not say in the first clause, "Which is a widow of isah [mixed lineage]? Any [family] into which an uncertain ḥalal has assimilated" — thus [we see that] an uncertain ḥalal is fit.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:4:1.english: However, a ḥalal [is] fit - Because of an uncertain ḥalal, [the Tanna] does not disqualify her.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:5:1.english: What is different [about] these - that their uncertainty disqualifies her.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:5:2.hebrew: דאורייתא - משום דוודאן פוסלין מן התורה בביאה, דנפקא לן ביבמות (דף סח.) מכי תהיה לאיש זר — כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה, פסלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:5:2.english: By Torah law - Because their definite [cases] disqualify [a woman from the priesthood] by Torah law through intercourse, as we derive in Yevamot (68a) from [the verse] "If she be to a strange man" — once she has had intercourse with someone who is unfit for her, he has disqualified her.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:5:3.hebrew: חלל נמי - ודאי פסול מדאוריית', דילפינן לה התם מ"לא יחלל זרעו": מקיש זרעו לו — מה הוא פוסל בביאתו, אף זרעו פוסל. והוא גופיה נפקא לן מ"לא יחלל": שני חילולין במשמע — אחד לזרעו ואחד לאשתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:5:3.english: A ḥalal also - [is] certainly a disqualification by Torah law, for we derive it there from "he shall not profane his offspring": [Scripture] compares his offspring to him — just as he disqualifies [a woman] through his intercourse, so too his offspring disqualifies [her]. And [as for] himself, we derive [it] from "he shall not profane": two profanations are implied — one for his offspring and one for his wife.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:6:1.hebrew: ר"ש בן אלעזר כו' - סיפא דמילתיה ארישא דמילתיה פריך, דקתני סיפא אין מכירין חללין שביניהן — משמע אפשר שהיה חלל אבל לא היו מכירין בו, אלמא אית ליה דפסיל. ורישא אמר איזוהי אלמנת עיסה, והכשיר כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:6:1.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, etc. - [The Gemara] is raising an objection from the latter clause of his statement against the first clause of his statement: for the latter clause teaches, "[Jews] do not identify the ḥalalin among them" — implying [that] it is possible there was a ḥalal [among them], only they did not identify him, thus he holds that [a ḥalal] disqualifies [her]; yet in the first clause he said, "Who is a widow of [a family of] mixed lineage [almanat isa]?" and deemed fit any [family] into which a person of uncertain ḥalal status was assimilated.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:1.hebrew: אמר ר' יוחנן ממזר צווח וחלל שותק איכא בינייהו - אדם שכשקורין אותו ממזר הוא צווח, וכשקורין אותו חלל שותק, איכא בין ר"מ לת"ק, ובין תנא קמא דברייתא אליבא דר"מ ור"ש בן אלעזר אליבא דר"מ:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A mamzer screaming and a ḥalal silent is between them - A person who, when they call him a mamzer, screams [in protest], and when they call him a ḥalal, is silent, is [the point of difference] between Rabbi Meir and the first tanna, and between the first tanna of the baraita according to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar according to Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:2.hebrew: תנא קמא סבר כל פסול דקרו ליה ושתיק פסול - דהודאה היא. וכל שאין בה לא משום ממזרות כו' דקאמר, אשתיקות קאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:2.english: The first tanna holds [that] anyone whom they call unfit and he is silent is unfit - For [silence] is an admission. And [that] which he says, "in which there is neither on account of mamzerut, etc.," refers to [cases of] silence.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:3.english: And this is what [he] is saying: Who is the widow of a [family of] questionable lineage - To declare [her] fit [to marry a priest].

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:4.hebrew: כל שאין בה לא שתוק ממזרות ולא שתוק נתינות - וכיון דתלה טעמא בשתיקה, הוא הדין לכל שתוקי פסול, ולא הוצרך למנות את כולם. ובאיזו הכשירו? באשת ספק חלל, שאנו מכירין את ספיקו שנתגרשה אמו ספק; אבל מי שאין מכירין בו, ושמענו שפוסלין אותו ושותק — פסול:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:7:4.english: Any [family] that has neither silence [regarding] mamzer status nor silence [regarding] Gibeonite status - And since [the first tanna] hung the reason on silence, the same law applies to all [cases of] silence [regarding] unfitness, and [thus] he did not need to enumerate all of them. And in which [case] did they declare [her] fit? In [the case of] the wife of a doubtful ḥalal, where we know his doubt — that his mother was doubtfully divorced; but one about whom we do not know [the circumstances], and we heard that [people] disqualify him and he is silent — [he is] unfit.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:8:1.hebrew: וקאמר ליה ר"מ - דוקא הני, אבל שתוק חלל לא פסול:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:8:1.english: And Rabbi Meir is saying to him - Specifically these [are disqualified], but one who is silent [when called] a ḥalal is not disqualified.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:8:2.hebrew: והא דשתיק - לאו משום דאודי, אלא משום דלא איכפת ליה, הואיל ולאו פסול קהל הוא. והיינו דקאמר: כל שאין בה אחד מכל אלו שתיקות, משיאין בנותיהן לכהונה, ואפי' יש בו שתוק חלל:
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:8:2.english: And [the fact] that he is silent - Not because he conceded, rather because he does not care, since it is not a disqualification from [entering] the congregation. And this is what [it] says: Any [family] in which there is not one of all these silences, they may marry their daughters into the priesthood — and even if there is in it a silence [regarding] a ḥalal.

Rashi on Ketubot 14b:9:1.hebrew: וקאמר ליה ר"ש לתנא קמא - לאו לתנא קמא דברייתא קאמר, דההיא רבנן היא, אלא לתנא ששנה דברי ר"מ בבית המדרש ואמר בשם ר"מ: שמעתי כל שאין בה כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 14b:9:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon is saying to the first tanna - He is not speaking to the first tanna of the baraita, for that [opinion] is [the view of] the Rabbis; rather, [he is speaking] to the tanna who recited the words of Rabbi Meir in the study hall and said in the name of Rabbi Meir: "I heard: 'Any [such family] that does not have...,' etc."

Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:13:1.hebrew: כמאן, אי כר"ג אפילו ברוב פסולין נמי מכשר - וא"ת: והא לא מכשר ברוב פסולין אלא כשטוענת ברי, ואית לה מיגו דאי בעיא אמרה "לא נבעלתי", או בלא מגו היכא דאיכא למימר בודקת ומזנה; אבל הכא, אפילו טוענת ברי — הא לית לה מגו, וליכא למימר בודקת ומזנה, דהא נאנסה. ואפי' אם נאמר דהכא לא ראוה שנאנסה, אלא היא אמרה כן, דאית לה מגו — א"כ תקשי הלכתא אהלכתא: דלקמן פסיק רב הלכה כר' יוסי, ולעיל פסיק רב יהודה אמר שמואל הלכה כר"ג. ואין נראה לומר דפליגי, דא"כ מאי מייתי אעובדא דארוס וארוסתו מרב יהודה אמר שמואל? וכן לעיל (כתובות דף יג.) פריך הלכתא אהלכתא: "קי"ל כרב נחמן בדיני כו'" — ואדרבה, הא רב פסיק כר' יהושע וקי"ל כרב באיסורי. ויש לומר דהכי פירושו: "כמאן? אי כר"ג" — ובטוענת ברי ובלא ראוה שנאנסה, דאיכא מגו — "אפילו ברוב פסולים נמי מכשר"; ואיירי נמי כשראוה מדברת, דאי לא ראוה מדברת, מאי פריך "אי כרבי יהושע, אפילו ברוב כשרים נמי פסול"? ומשני: "אמר רב, בקרונות של צפורי היה מעשה כו'". פי': לעולם דלא טענה ברי, ור' יוחנן בן נורי בתרוייהו — היכא דלא טענה ברי לכ"ע בעינן תרי רובי. והא דלא קאמר בשינויא "לעולם דלא טענה ברי", משום דבאתקפתא לא קאמר "אי בטוענת ברי כו'". אי נמי, נוכל לפרש דבשינויא נמי איירי בברי ודאיכא מגו, ולא תקשי הלכתא אהלכתא: דדוקא דיעבד פסיק שמואל כר"ג, כדאמר לעיל: "ואת לא תעביד עובדא עד דאיכא רוב כשרין". אף על גב דלעיל משמע דברוב אחד שרי לכתחלה, רב חייא בר אשי סבר דלכתחלה בעינן תרי רובי, ומתני' קתני "הרי זו תנשא" דמשמע לכתחלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:13:1.english: "In accordance with whose [opinion]? If in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, even in a majority of unfit [men] he deems [her] fit" - And if you ask: Surely [Rabban Gamliel] only deems [her] fit in a majority of unfit [men] when she makes a certain claim and has a migo — since if she wanted, she could have said, "I did not have intercourse" — or without a migo where one can say she checks [with whom she has intercourse] and acts promiscuously; but here, even if she makes a certain claim, she has no migo, and one cannot say she checks and acts promiscuously, since she was violated! And even if we say that here they did not see her being violated, rather she herself said so, such that she has a migo — if so, there is a contradiction between one halakhah and another: for below Rav rules that the halakhah follows Rabbi Yose, whereas above Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel that the halakhah follows Rabban Gamliel. And it does not seem right to say that they disagree, for if so, why does [the Gemara] bring [a proof] regarding the incident of a betrothed man and his betrothed from Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel? And similarly above (Ketubot 13a) it asks [about] a contradiction between one halakhah and another: "We hold like Rav Naḥman in monetary matters, etc." — on the contrary, Rav rules like Rabbi Yehoshua, and we hold like Rav in ritual matters. And one can say that this is its explanation: "In accordance with whose [opinion]? If in accordance with Rabban Gamliel" — i.e., where she makes a certain claim and they did not see her being violated, so that there is a migo — "even in a majority of unfit [men] he deems [her] fit"; and it is also speaking of a case where they saw her speaking [with a man], for if they did not see her speaking [with anyone], why does [the Gemara] ask, "If in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, even in a majority of fit [men] he deems [her] unfit"? And [the Gemara] answers: "Rav said: The incident occurred by the wagons of Tzippori, etc." Explanation: Actually, [our Mishnah is a case] where she does not make a certain claim, and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri [requires] both [majorities] — [for] where she does not make a certain claim, according to everyone we require two majorities. And the reason [the Gemara] did not say in the answer, "Actually, where she does not make a certain claim," is because in the objection it did not say, "If where she makes a certain claim, etc." Alternatively, we can explain that in the answer as well it is speaking of a certain claim and where there is a migo, and there is no contradiction between one halakhah and another: for Shmuel only ruled like Rabban Gamliel post facto, as he said above, "And you should not act [on this ruling] unless there is a majority of fit [men]." Even though above it implies that with one majority it is permitted ab initio, Rav Ḥiya bar Ashi holds that ab initio we require two majorities, and the Mishnah teaches, "Behold, she may marry," which implies ab initio.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:4:1.hebrew: לא משום ממזרות כו' - הא דלא חשיב עמוני ומואבי, משום דלא פסיקא, דזכרים אסורין ונקבות מותרות. ומצרי ואדומי לא חשיב, דאינן אסורין אלא עד דור שלישי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:4:1.english: Neither due to mamzer status, etc. - That which [the baraita] does not list an Ammonite or a Moabite is because [the rule] is not uniform, as males are forbidden and females are permitted. And it does not list an Egyptian or an Edomite, as they are only forbidden until the third generation.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:6:1.hebrew: ותו ר"ש בן אלעזר אומר איזוהי עיסה כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל והאמרת רישא חלל כשר - ה"ג בכל הספרים ובפירוש ר"ח. ומפרש: "כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל" — הא ודאי חלל פסול, "והא אמרת רישא חלל כשר" — והיינו ודאי חלל. ואין נראה, דמאי פריך מתנא קמא? דלמא ת"ק פליג עליה! ופירוש הקונטרס וגרסתו עיקר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:6:1.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Who is [the widow of a family of] questionable lineage? Any [family] in which a doubtful ḥalal was assimilated; but didn't you say [in] the first clause [that] a ḥalal is fit? - This is the reading in all the texts and in the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel. And he explains: "Any [family] in which a doubtful ḥalal was assimilated" — [this implies that if] a definite ḥalal [was assimilated], she is unfit; "but didn't you say [in] the first clause [that] a ḥalal is fit?" — and that refers to a definite ḥalal. However, [this] does not seem [correct], for how can [the Gemara] raise an objection from the first Tanna? Perhaps the first Tanna disagrees with him! And the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] and his reading are primary.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:7:1.hebrew: ממזר צווח וחלל שותק איכא בינייהו - תימה, דהוה ליה למימר: "ממזר צווח ושותק, וחלל שותק איכא בינייהו", דבממזר שותק נמי פליגי, דהא מכשר ליה ר"ש בן אלעזר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:7:1.english: [The case of one called] mamzer who protests and [one called] ḥalal who is silent is [the difference] between them - This is astonishing, for he should have said: "[The cases of one called] mamzer who protests and [one called mamzer] who is silent, and [one called] ḥalal who is silent, are [the difference] between them," since they also disagree regarding [one called] mamzer who is silent, for Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar declares him fit.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:9:1.hebrew: אבל ממזר צווח וחלל שותק פסול - וא"ת: ממזר צווח מנא ליה דפסל ר"ש בן אלעזר? ואומר ר"י: מדקתני במילתיה "איזוהי עיסה? כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל", דלא הוה ליה למימר אלא "מכירין ישראל ממזרים שביניהם, ואין מכירין חללין שביניהם", דמינה שמעינן בחלל צווח דכשר — כי היכי דלא הוצרך להשמיענו "כל שנטמע בה ספק ממזר". אלא ודאי אתא למידק: דחלל צווח דוקא כשר, הא ממזר צווח — פסול:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:9:1.english: However, [if he is called] mamzer and screams [in protest], or ḥalal and is silent, he is unfit - And if you ask: From where does he [derive] that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar disqualifies [a case of] mamzer and screams [in protest]? And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: From the fact that [Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar] taught in his statement, "What is an isah [a family of uncertain lineage]? Any [family] in which a possible ḥalal has been intermingled" — for he needed only to say, "Israel recognizes the mamzerim among them, and does not recognize the ḥalalim among them," from which we [already] infer regarding a ḥalal who screams [in protest] that he is fit — just as he did not need to teach us, "any [family] in which a possible mamzer has been intermingled." Rather, he certainly came to imply that specifically a ḥalal who screams [in protest] is fit, whereas a mamzer who screams [in protest] is unfit.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:9:2.hebrew: מסתייה דלא מפקינן ליה מקהל - וא"ת: מה צריך להאי טעמא? לימא הא דשתיק משום דאודויי קא מודי! דהא ממזר שותק פסול לת"ק משום דשתיקה כהודאה, וה"ה דחלל שותק לר"ש דפסול מהאי טעמא, ואע"ג דגבי ממזר שותק לדידיה לא הוי שתיקה כהודאה — היינו משום דסבר דממזר קלא אית ליה! וי"ל דהכי פירושא: סבר מסתייה דלא מפקינן ליה מקהל (כהונה) — פי' אפי' מקהל כהונה; אע"פ שזה מחרפו וקורהו חלל, סבור דאין מוציאין אותו מקהל כהונה, וסבור: אם יצווח, יחזרו לברר הדבר ויפסלוהו. וטעם זה שייך גם בממזר שותק לת"ק, ולא נאמר דשתיקה כהודאה. וכן פירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14b:9:2.english: It is sufficient for him that we do not expel him from the congregation - And if you ask: Why is this reason necessary? Let us say that [the reason] he is silent is because he is admitting [it]! For [one who is called] a mamzer and is silent is unfit according to the first tanna because silence is like admission, and the same applies to [one who is called] a ḥalal who is silent according to Rabbi Shimon — that he is unfit for that reason; and even though regarding [one who is called] a mamzer who is silent, for him silence is not [deemed] like admission, that is because he holds that a mamzer generates publicity! And one can answer that this is its explanation: he holds it is sufficient for him that we do not expel him from the congregation (of priesthood) — meaning, even from the congregation of priesthood; even though this [person] insults him and calls him a ḥalal, he thinks that they do not remove him from the congregation of priesthood, and he thinks [that] if he cries out [in protest], they will go back and investigate the matter and disqualify him. And this reason applies also to [one who is called] a mamzer who is silent according to the first tanna, and we do not say that silence is like admission. And so Rashi explained.
